(22 February 2014) | longest wins = [[Sydney FC]], [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne Heart]] (5) | longest unbeaten = [[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]], [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne Heart]] (7) | longest winless = [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne Heart]] (14) | longest losses = [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne Heart]] (5) | highest attendance = 45,202 | lowest attendance = 5,046 | average attendance = 13,041 ([[Image:Green Arrow Up.svg|12px]] 700) | prevseason = [[2012–13 A-League|2012–13]] | nextseason = [[2014–15 A-League|2014–15]] }} The '''2013–14 A-League''' was the 37th season of top-flight soccer in [[Australia]], and the ninth of the [[A-League]] since its establishment in 2004. The season began on 11 October 2013, with [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]] as the defending A-League Premiers and [[Central Coast Mariners FC|Central Coast Mariners]] as the defending A-League Champions. The regular season concluded on 13 April 2014, with [[Brisbane Roar FC|Brisbane Roar]] crowned Premiers. The [[2014 A-League Grand Final|2014 Grand Final]] took place on 4 May 2014, with Brisbane Roar claiming their third Championship with a 2–1 win in [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] against Western Sydney Wanderers.{{cite web|title=Henrique scores winner as Roar claim title in thriller|url=http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news-display/Henrique-scores-winner-as-Brisbane-Roar-claim-title-in-thriller/90290|publisher=[[Football Federation Australia]]|access-date=8 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504122106/http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news-display/Henrique-scores-winner-as-Brisbane-Roar-claim-title-in-thriller/90290|archive-date=4 May 2014|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} This was the first A-League season to be broadcast on free-to-air television, after [[Special Broadcasting Service|SBS]] obtained the rights to a live Friday night game each week of the season, and all finals games on a one-hour delay, on a $160 million four-year broadcast deal.{{cite web|title=Football returns to free-to-air TV on SBS|url=http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/news/1129433/football-returns-to-free-to-air-tv-on-sbs|publisher=theworldgame.sbs.com.au|access-date=16 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130306075631/http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/news/1129433/Football-returns-to-free-to-air-TV-on-SBS|archive-date=6 March 2013|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}{{cite web|title=FFA shores up the game's TV future|url=http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/a-league/news/1129455/ffa-shores-up-the-game's-tv-future|publisher=theworldgame.sbs.com.au|access-date=16 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121129080625/http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/a-league/news/1129455/ffa-shores-up-the-game%27s-tv-future|archive-date=29 November 2012|url-status=dead}} {{TOC limit|limit=3}} ==Clubs== {{A-League 2012–2014 map}} {{Further|A-League#Clubs}} {| class="wikitable" |- !
